prompt: Build a minecraft based world where we attack giants by swinging through the air with swords

foundation.why: A block world and block-built bodies are the blocky kind; giants that come in a round or a run. A block world is a world in the registry, not a loop that stays: the prompt asks for a fight, not for saved building.

checklist.text: The loop's requirements ledger holds every essential of the prompt in the creator's own words, each with a home (exists, build or probe); no line is cut that the creator did not cut, and nothing is narrowed or deferred because the kit lacks it
The locked spec's runtime, profile, loop and kind are among this case's foundation.accept, and the ledger names the lines that decided each
All six gates pass on the delivered game, each verdict naming what ran and what it skipped

The delivery carries the promise ledger: every build promise and every core ledger line proven by the play-test, or named as failed, untested or unreachable; if anything failed, the delivery says so first
Nobody touched the run between the prompt and the delivered version: no file edited by hand, no step re-run by a person, no answer beyond the case's answers
The world is built of blocks (ground, cliffs, trees, buildings) and reads as a block-building game's world, with block faces that stay crisp up close, far away and at speed
The players' characters are block-built too, and match the world
Players fly by swinging: hooks fired at the world, a rope that swings them, a reel and a boost; chained swings carry a player across the map without touching the ground
The swing passes the kit's own measured feel checks (a rope never keeps slack, a full reel arrives and stops, the hero stays on screen and does not shake)
The enemies are giants: at least five times a player's height, more than one in a round, and they come at the players or at what the players defend
Players attack the giants with swords from the air: a strike made at speed hurts a giant, and a giant can be killed
A new player knows what to do within the first minute without reading anything long: where to go, how to fly, what to hit
Nothing on screen names or copies the named block game or any other franchise: every picture, texture and model is ours or licensed
Played side by side with the private prototype the creator accepted on 2026-10-10 ("great, I love it"), the creator says this game is of that quality (creator's judgement)
With 2 players, each screen shows the other player as a character with a nameplate, where they really are, swinging on their own hooks
A round ends on a results screen (won or lost) and replays
The player body and one block texture swap through slots with no code change
Every visible thing is a slot

control.text: The game includes a working fishing minigame

note: The creator's bridge of 2026-10-10, re-created for spec v2 on 2026-10-13: "Give nothing but the prompt ..., and output something of this quality." The prompt is verbatim. The quality bar is a private prototype on a third party's code that never ships; builders never open it.
